title: Grateful Dead Live at Star Theatre on 1970-03-08
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with solid clarity captures a memorable acoustic set highlighted by an exquisite Black Peter and Lovelight, though the on‑stage guest vocalist makes Not Fade Away a mixed moment.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its strong acoustic work—Black Peter’s heartfelt solo and the seamless NFA → Lovelight transition are repeatedly called out as highlights. While the soundboard source provides generally good, listenable audio (aside from occasional volume spikes from the guest singer), many reviewers note that the bizarre on‑stage vocalist detracts from parts of Not Fade Away and some improvisations.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews rate the performance 4–5 stars and describe good soundboard quality; a few low‑star comments focus on the disruptive guest vocalist, leading to an overall strong but not flawless rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and listenable with nice acoustic detail; occasional volume fluctuations when the guest vocalist gets loud, but no major drop‑outs or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows well, featuring a strong acoustic segment that leads into the NFA → Lovelight transition; despite chaotic moments with audience members and the guest singer, the band maintains composure and tight playing throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocal tone on Black Peter is described as sweet and heartbreaking; guitar work praised during acoustic solo.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals noted as crystal clear; praised for his contribution to the overall sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are called tight, providing a solid rhythmic foundation.
